cards.title: AI demand rebounds; rates still bite
cards.question: Is the rebound a regime shift or relief?
cards.prompt: As of Nov 12 2026 compare 7/30/90-day Nasdaq, SOXX, RSP, IWM and yields. Reuters Nov 11 reports Nasdaq +1.60%, S&P +1.31% after CoreWeave earnings; Nov 10 CPI lifted rate expectations. Separate facts from hypothesis; invalidate recovery if breadth fades and yields rise. Sources: https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/global-markets-global-markets-2026-11-11/ and https://www.reuters.com/world/china/global-markets-wrapup-1-2026-11-10/

cards.title: Positioning reset, not all-clear
cards.question: Can participation outlast short-covering?
cards.prompt: Review Reuters Nov 11 positioning report: tech positioning below April 2025 lows and weaker retail call buying. Contrast Nov 11 Nasdaq +1.60%, Russell +0.9%, and 7/30-day breadth. Hypothesis: positioning supports a bounce; reject if equal-weight and small caps weaken. https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/after-us-market-shake-out-signs-suggest-too-soon-say-worst-is-over-2026-11-11/

cards.title: Chip demand is measurable
cards.question: Does foundry growth become profitable AI usage?
cards.selfCheck: Check TSMC sales and cloud margins.
cards.prompt: Use TSMC Nov 10 release: October NT$586.89B +59.7% YoY, Jan-Oct +43.3%. Compare with CoreWeave Nov 10 Q3 revenue $3.661B, 10% adjusted operating margin and net losses. Foundry growth is fact; sustained end-customer ROI is hypothesis. Check utilization and margins; reject if orders or pricing deteriorate. https://pr.tsmc.com/english/news/3349 https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Reports-Strong-Third-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx

cards.title: Old financing meets new capacity
cards.question: Will August's loan support profitable 2027 deployments?
cards.prompt: Trace CoreWeave's Aug 10 2026 $2.6B DDTL 5.5 financing (SOFR +5.50%, ~5-year loan against ~3-year customer contracts) to Nov 10 Q3 contracted power >4.6GW vs active >1.7GW, backlog $132.5B. Financing is confirmed; renewal and ROI are hypotheses. Watch conversion, renewals and interest burden. https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Closes-2-6-Billion-Loan-Facility-Expanding-Financing-Flexibility-for-AI-Infrastructure/default.aspx

cards.title: December tests demand and rates
cards.question: Which December data could reset 2027 assumptions?
cards.prompt: Official Fed calendar lists Dec 8-9 2026 FOMC; TSMC investor calendar lists Nov sales on Dec 10 2026. Bull: rate expectations stabilize and foundry demand holds. Bear: higher yields and weaker sales/guidance. Note market already prices substantial AI growth and tighter policy; verify releases before drawing conclusions. https://www.chicagofed.org/utilities/about-us/federal-reserve-calendars https://investor.tsmc.com/english/financial-calendar

cards.title: Orders are real; returns unproven
cards.question: Can AI suppliers beat debt-funded builders?
cards.prompt: Set a 30-90-day falsifiable test from Nov 12: compare MU/TSMC and optical/semicap supplier earnings revisions with CRWV and other financed operators, plus relative returns. CoreWeave Nov 10 raised 2026 revenue guidance to $13.0-13.3B and capex to $37-39B, with Q4 interest expense guided $1.05-1.15B. Hypothesis: suppliers outperform if utilization and financing lag. Reject on supplier order cuts or improving operator free cash flow. https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Reports-Strong-Third-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx
